newsitem.title: GREECE: PRESS DIGEST - GREEK GENERAL NEWS- NOV 20.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - GREEK GENERAL NEWS- NOV 20.

text.p: Leading stories in the Greek
general press:
KATHIMERINI
--The demands of convergence have led the government to opt
for a wage freeze in both the private and public sector in its
ambitious effort to bring inflation down to 4.5 percent by the
end of 1997.
--Fear and loathing in the money markets, as bankers react
against the government's proposed interbank tax.
--Turkish warplanes repeatedly violated Greek airspace
yesterday as Greek and Turkish officials crossed swords at the
Western European Union council in Belgium.
--Main opposition New Democracy honourary president
Constantine Mitsotakis throws out barbs at ND leader Miltiades
Evert's tactics in Parliament.
ELEFTHEROTYPIA
--Wage-earners and pensioners respond with strikes to the
government's plans for cost-of-living increases.
--Dimitra Liani-Papandreou, the widow of late founder and
president of ruling party PASOK Andreas Papandreou, tells
reporters that her husband's doctors knew he was receiving
homeopathic medicines.
TA NEA
--Wage increases with the dropper as well as seven new taxes
in the new budget announced yesterday.
--Liani-Papandreou testifies to prosecutor over her claims
that her phones were tapped.
ETHNOS
--State subsidies for businesses are expected to create
10,000 places for young unemployed. Changes afoot to the law on
public sector appointments.
ELEFTHEROS TYPOS
--The death of a nine-year-old student on the roads of
Athens has prompted local mothers to do their own policing of
the roads.
--Maria Petrakis, Athens Newsroom +301 3311812-4
